tasks.title: Delete the Millis and Seconds aliases from loop
acceptance: these are bare number aliases whose own doc says they guard nothing, and they are the VECTOR for a false claim that a branded duration exists

kit.json lists them among loop exports alphabetized beside Loop and Scheduler, one package away from core EpochMillis, with nothing distinguishing a type that guards from a synonym for number — and agents read the manifest first, because AGENTS.md tells them to
36 type positions; every use site field name already ends in Ms or Seconds, so the deletion is mechanical
this is the actual cause and the cheapest fix in the set
tasks.notes: The prose was never the failure — four documents stated the truth, two of them in the source of the packages involved, and the false claim was written twice anyway.

tasks.title: tools/gallery.mjs — enforce the logic cap the rule now states
acceptance: print each exhibit logic/art split and fail the one over 200 logic code lines

classification is per MODULE via an @art tag in the header doc comment, per GALLERY.md — a module is art if deleting it changes only what the exhibit looks or sounds like, holds no state past a frame, and moves no number the player is playing for
ambiguity resolves to logic. Until this tool exists the grep in GALLERY.md is the rule, which means the rule is currently unenforced
also worth a lint rule for the one lintable piece: every duration parameter name ends in Ms or Seconds, which catches the after(3000)-means-fifty-minutes class

tasks.title: DepthSorter needs a sorted flag — it is the only thing blocking a whole invariant
acceptance: the shared Bucket cannot meet its invariant B7 — "an unsorted each throws" — from outside the package, and the reason is worth reading: DepthSorter publishes nothing that separates "not sorted" from "sorted, nothing culled"

pre-sort, count equals the bucket count and indexAt(i) === i — and an unculled frame filled in depth order is BIT-IDENTICAL to that. Any detector built on the published surface is a false alarm on a real frame
a public `sorted` flag, lowered by add and clear and raised by sort, is three lines and unblocks it
the bucket test already asserts the gap as a tripwire, so whoever adds the flag is told where to come back
tasks.notes: A helper outside the package could not close it, and said so rather than shipping a detector that would cry wolf. That is the right call and it routes here. Closed 2026-08-18 after verifying in the tree: DepthSorter carries the sorted flag; 25 references in packages/iso/src/depth.ts and bucket invariant B7 passes.

tasks.title: The waypost flag can reach isoWall's new refusal
acceptance: the flag animates sway into BOTH coordinates in proportion, which is edge-on exactly when sway is 0 — and isoWall now throws rather than silently drawing nothing

it does not fire today, and the check for that was thorough: core noise2 returns exactly 0 at 397k of 14M lattice samples, but only when BOTH inputs are lattice points, and the phase here is fractional — 0 exact zeros in 200k samples
move the sway onto one axis rather than relying on a fractional phase nobody will remember is load-bearing
two neighboring sprites were checked and are safe by construction — their wave would have to reach 1.2 and 0.52 against ranges of 0.12 and 0.17
tasks.notes: The one shape in the repo that can reach the new throw. Safe by accident is not safe.

tasks.title: The size tool sums two backends no consumer ships together
acceptance: draw is the only package with two mutually exclusive backends: a browser game ships canvas2d and not record, a headless replay ships record and not canvas2d
the gate reads their sum, which is a bundle nobody downloads — 12.93 against a real 12.08 or 11.30

this is the same species as the adapter finding already fixed, but the fix is different: an adapter IS downloaded by a game and must stay counted, whereas mutually exclusive backends genuinely cannot both ship
decide whether the tool should report a per-entry-point figure, and note that getting this right retires draw's override rather than merely explaining it

tasks.title: The hero carries no @art tags, so the tool cannot see its split
acceptance: npm run gallery reports the hero as 1286 logic / 99 art, where GALLERY.md documents 622 / 768 — because not one module in examples/demo/src carries an @art tag
the tag goes on its own line inside the file leading doc comment: sprites, sky, ambient, sound, palette are the candidates

the classification test is the one in GALLERY.md — a module is art if deleting it changes only what the exhibit looks or sounds like, holds no state past a frame, and moves no number the player is playing for
the hero is exempt from the CAP, not from being measured. A documented split nothing can verify is the same species as the claim that a duration alias guarded anything
tasks.notes: Found by tools/gallery.mjs the moment it could measure. The tool says so explicitly rather than printing a large number and moving on. Closed 2026-08-18 after verifying in the tree: Five modules in examples/demo/src carry @art; npm run gallery reports the hero at 682 logic / 872 art with no warning.

tasks.title: LightField falloff's plateau is a hard ring, so every value but 1 seams
acceptance: falloff is documented as a plateau — '2 holds full intensity to half the radius' — and Surface.softEllipse has stops only at 0 and r, so pool() cannot ramp FROM the plateau edge; it restarts the ramp at full intensity from the center
the observable: at falloff 2 alpha steps ~0.95 to ~0.45 at exactly r/2, so every pool wears a hard elliptical rim and adjacent rims cross into the seam the light field exists to avoid
verified both directions by the caverns exhibit: at ?lightFalloff=4 two braziers show crossing crescents; at 1 the same pair merge into one region with no rim and no ridge
fix is an inner-stop radius on softEllipse, or documenting 1 as the only seamless value and saying why — the doc must not describe a plateau the code cannot produce
tasks.notes: Found by examples/caverns, the first real consumer of draw.light. The exhibit ships falloff 1 plus a two-call core/halo nest as its workaround.

tasks.title: SpriteDef.emit receives no clock, so nothing emissive can move
acceptance: emit's parameters are (field, gx, gy, v, rng, zPx): no pen, no t. A guttering torch, a breathing crystal or a lamp being switched on cannot be written through the sanctioned hook
two exhibits independently routed around it via pen.light?.add inside animate — caverns and island — which is what makes it a gap rather than a preference
the kit requires something to move on everything (draw invariant, GALLERY.md rule 3), so a hook for emission that cannot animate is dead API for the common case
either emit takes the frame time, or the docs name animate as the place emissive motion belongs and emit is documented as static-only
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns; corroborated independently by examples/island.

tasks.title: LightField.begin(darkness) is write-only, against non-negotiable 11
acceptance: scale, falloff and bloom all read back under their own names; darkness — the number deciding whether there is a night at all — does not
so every exhibit with a day cycle holds the only copy of it, which is exactly the shadow copy non-negotiable 11 exists to remove
a getter over private state costs three lines, has no policy attached, and cannot break an invariant — the rule’s own words
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns. Non-negotiable 11 was added after light.ts was written, so this is a rule that arrived late rather than one that was ignored.

tasks.title: bootstrap exposes no clock, so every exhibit invents one
acceptance: ui.createOverlay({ now }) wants milliseconds and performance.now() is banned in exhibit src, so an exhibit needing an overlay has no sanctioned clock
caverns used () => boot.loop.realTime * 1000; island wrote performance.now() anyway, which is the lint rule catching what the API should have prevented
Boot.now would be one line, and bootstrap already exists precisely to remove the steps that are silent when wrong
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns. The island case is the evidence that documentation would not have been enough.

tasks.title: input has no hover gesture, so a cursor-following anything is inexpressible
acceptance: GestureMap carries tap, longpress, three drags and zoom — no pointermove

caverns wanted a light that follows the cursor, the most obvious interaction for that exhibit, and shipped tap instead; terraces highlights the tile under the cursor and had to reach past the gesture surface for it

decide it deliberately: either hover joins the map, or the omission is documented with the reason (a hover has no touch equivalent, and an input package that pretends otherwise makes desktop-only games by accident)
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns, corroborated by examples/terraces.

tasks.title: the placement pass is where near-field world art has to live, and its name says otherwise
acceptance: near-field world material — a ceiling band, motes, a carried lantern — must composite BELOW the light field; overlay is above it, so placement is the only pass left
placement is documented as the ghost and the selection rim, so every exhibit with foreground art files it under a name that describes a different job
either the pass is renamed for what it is, or a pass is added below the light composite for world art that is not sorted
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns.

tasks.title: ui.roll animates toward a target, which makes it wrong for a number under test
acceptance: a 200-unit jump took about 10 s to settle, so a diagnostic readout displays a wrong number for the whole interval a viewer is looking at it
the roll is right for gold and wrong for a count under test, and the gallery now puts a worst-frame and a live count in every HUD — so the diagnostic case is no longer rare
wants either a snap mode or a second primitive; the exhibit kept the roll because GALLERY.md rule 7 requires the HUD to be ui, which is the rule working and the widget not
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/caverns. Directly caused by the cost row added to GALLERY.md the same day.

tasks.title: An animated color turns a shared ramp cache into a global allocator
acceptance: rampFor keys on the exact (inner, outer) Rgba pair with no quantization, so a color varying continuously with time misses every frame; a miss allocates a canvas element, a context, a gradient and a fill

eviction is wholesale — if (ramps.size >= RAMP_LIMIT) ramps.clear() — so ONE animated color destroys every other call site’s entries: contact shadows, light pools, sky and sprites all use constant colors and become misses as collateral

measured live in examples/crowd by wrapping createRadialGradient, which is only reached on a miss: 3.74 misses/frame, 4053 over 1083 frames, a full cache drop every ~26 frames, ~225 canvas elements/sec, ~3.7 MB/s of GC feed
non-negotiable 7 says the hot path allocates nothing, and it was allocating inside draw at 3.7 MB/s
the trap sits two layers below the author: an exhibit calls glowDot, which calls softEllipse, which consults a cache the author has never heard of and whose constraint no signature states
fix: quantize inside rampFor to what a 64px ramp can resolve, evict one entry rather than all, and state the residual constraint in Surface.softEllipse’s doc
RAMP_LIMIT's comment already anticipated this case and chose the one remedy that punishes the innocent call sites; the new comment should record that, since it is the instructive half
tasks.notes: Found by examples/crowd while hunting its own 23ms tail. Its workaround — snapping only the color to nine levels in an @art module — took misses from 3.74/frame to 0.003 and is removable once the package fix lands. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: rampFor quantizes its key and evicts per entry; 16 references in canvas2d.ts.

tasks.title: worstFrameMs cannot see a GC pause between pumps, and the gallery is judged on it
acceptance: loop.stats.worstFrameMs measures the pump’s own wall time only (endMs - nowMs), so a pause landing between pumps never appears in it
GALLERY.md § Scale’s cost row makes this figure the number every exhibit is gated on, and it is blind to precisely the failure K39 turned out to be
crowd saw 23.1ms on one machine and 13.1ms on another for the same build, which is the symptom: whether the pause lands inside a pump is machine-dependent and the readout is not
a second figure from requestAnimationFrame deltas would catch it; at minimum PERFORMANCE.md must say that a green worstFrameMs is not proof of no hitch
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/crowd. Directly undermines a gate added to GALLERY.md the same day, which is why it is not merely a docs task. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: loop ships stats.worstGapMs, which sees a pause between pumps; 9 references in loop.ts.

tasks.title: Nothing can ask whether a point would be culled without inserting it
acceptance: GALLERY.md § Scale tells every exhibit to cull before the sort; DepthSorter offers no way to ask the question without insert-then-discard
the alternative is hand-rolling HALF_W / HALF_H and the footprint-to-world-rect projection that depth.ts #cull already inlines, inside exhibit code, which puts projection constants in a game
crowd declined to cull 560 off-screen walkers for exactly this reason and said so
an isPointVisible(gx, gy, heightPx, radius) shaped against Camera would make the advice reachable from an exhibit in one line
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/crowd. The advice it blocks is a rule this repo wrote, so the gap is self-inflicted.

tasks.title: pathSample and pathDirAt each binary-search the same s
acceptance: a walker that needs both a position and a facing pays two searches over one arc-length table for one value of s
at 900 walkers that is 1800 searches a frame where 900 would do
wants either a combined call returning both, or a cursor a caller can carry across the pair
tasks.notes: Recorded first in crowd.ts by one agent and seconded by the next, independently. Not urgent at present frame times; cheap and known.

tasks.title: Every exhibit's opening worst-frame score is its warm-up cost
acceptance: the first ten-second window includes the page-load frame, so crowd reads ~16.3ms on arrival and settles to ~12.0ms from the second window on
truthful, and it means every exhibit in the gallery displays its worst number at the exact moment a visitor is deciding what they think
decide deliberately: discard the first N frames, start the window at the first steady frame, or label it — but not silently, because the cost row made this number the score
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/crowd. A consequence of the cost row rather than a pre-existing bug. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: stats.warmingUp is true while opening gaps are discarded, so a HUD shows a dash rather than a warm-up spike.

tasks.title: ActionEvent.gx/gy is a flat-ground answer, and elevation has no seam to correct it
acceptance: every ActionEvent carries gx/gy computed as though the ground were flat, and there is no way to hand input a HeightField so that it is not

SEAMS.md settles that iso does the math and input owns the gesture, and this is the case where that split has no wire: the gesture arrives, the math it needs is elevation-aware, and nothing carries the height field across

so a game with terrain gets a wrong tile from the default path and nothing warns it. examples/terraces measures the error at 281 px and 14-16 tiles on its own hillside, and demo shipped a 212-237 px version of the same bug
this is the exhibit terraces exists to demonstrate — and it is demonstrating a bug the kit ships by default rather than one a caller can make

decide the seam: either input takes an optional HeightField and gx/gy become terrain-aware, or ActionEvent stops offering gx/gy where a height field exists and the caller is routed to an iso call that requires one
whichever is chosen, the flat answer must not be the silent default on sloped ground
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/terraces, the first consumer of iso.height. The most serious correctness finding of the gallery phase: a silent wrong answer on the kit’s most common interaction. Closed 2026-08-18: input takes an optional terrain declaration; omitted now emits one flat-ground-pick diagnostic the first time a coordinate is read. iso gained worldToTileOnHeights.

tasks.title: renderFrame's terrain margin grows a box, but elevation only moves a tile along gx+gy
acceptance: the Terrain pass receives a tile box widened by maxHeightPx so a summit whose base is off-screen still paints — correct, and necessary
but height displaces a tile only along gx+gy, and the margin is applied to both axes of a box, so the widened region grows quadratically in a direction elevation never uses
measured in examples/terraces on terrain 1470 px tall: 26,569 tiles visited for a frame that paints 1,201

the exhibit works around it by walking u = gx+gy / v = gx-gy directly, reaching the same coverage in 3,081 visits — and notes that ascending u is strictly far-to-near, where row-major is only accidentally so
a pass that hands the caller a box costs every tall-terrain exhibit the same 8x. Either the margin follows the axis elevation actually uses, or the pass hands over the u/v walk
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/terraces while closing a 93.9 ms worst frame. Two thirds of that number was this.

tasks.title: HeightField.heights is a TileSource, which cannot be iterated
acceptance: a consumer that wants to walk the field — to paint it, to find its extremes, to build a derived map — can only sample it point by point through the accessor
examples/terraces hit this painting a hillside; examples/canyon steps a whole field every tick and will hit it harder
either TileSource gains an iteration contract or HeightField exposes its extent and a read path that does not cost a call per tile
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/terraces.

tasks.title: draw publishes no projection, so an exhibit that needs one re-derives it
acceptance: pen.snapX / pen.snapY exist and the transform they belong to is not published, so an exhibit placing anything by hand re-derives what the pen already knows
combines with K41: an exhibit told to cull before the sort must hand-roll HALF_W / HALF_H as well
the shape wanted is a read-only projection off the pen — world to screen and back, including the snap
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/terraces; overlaps K41 from examples/crowd, which asked for the same thing from the other side.

tasks.title: Camera cannot express "no bounds", and its default is not unbounded
acceptance: omitting bounds does not mean unbounded: the default is ±10,000 world px, about ±312 tiles, and its own comment calls that "effectively unbounded"
examples/endless crosses it in fourteen screens of travel
keepVisible clamps against bounds, so an author cannot escape by leaving bounds off — the two options are a wrong clamp or a made-up enormous number
the exhibit ships ±4e7 and says so in its source, which is a magic number standing in for a missing state
bounds: undefined should mean unbounded, and the current default should be either deleted or named as the opinion it is
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/endless, the first streaming consumer of iso. The comment calling ±10,000 effectively unbounded is the tell — it was true for every map that existed when it was written.

tasks.title: massing and animate receive different Rng streams, so an animator cannot re-derive its own shape
acceptance: a sprite whose massing chose a height and a lean cannot recover either in animate by drawing in the same order — it gets a different stream and therefore different numbers
so a moving crown sits beside the static one it is supposed to belong to. This is live today in examples/island/src/trees.ts, the palm, around lines 158-163
endless worked around it with toUnit(hashStep(v.seed, i)), which is position-in-variant addressing rather than stream order
the kit could offer exactly that as variantAt(v, i) — a value addressed by index, identical in both hooks, which is what both callers actually wanted
this compounds K33: emit has no clock, animate is the only place motion can live, and animate cannot see what massing decided
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/endless, with a live instance named in another exhibit’s source. Two hooks over one sprite that cannot agree on the sprite.

tasks.title: Streaming on render freezes the world in a background tab
acceptance: loop’s own table is right — pixels on render, anything that must not freeze on update — and endless shipped the bug first anyway
a streamed world is the first thing in this repo where the distinction is load-bearing rather than tidy, because the symptom is not a stutter but a world that stops existing
bootstrap exists to remove the steps that are silent when wrong, and this is one: it belongs in its header beside stepMs and the light field
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/endless, which reports having written it wrong before writing it right.

tasks.title: Every streaming game will write the same six lines of screen-diamond culling
acceptance: renderFrame’s visible box over-covers the screen diamond about 2x; free on a bounded map, 5,000 wasted tiles at the zoom-out limit on an edgeless one
a screen rect IS a pair of intervals in (gx+gy, gx-gy), which is six lines and the same insight terraces used to turn 26,569 tile visits into 3,081
two exhibits derived it independently within a day of each other, which is the threshold for it belonging in the package
lands with K41 and K45 — all three are the same missing thing seen from three sides: iso knows the projection and will not tell anyone
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/endless; the same arithmetic examples/terraces used for K45.

tasks.title: The light field is priced by pool area, and area scales with zoom squared
acceptance: a pool radius is given in tiles, so its screen area grows with the square of the zoom and a player pinching in multiplies the field’s fill cost without adding a light
this is the variable that reconciles two measurements that looked contradictory: caverns at 704 pools for ~0.2 ms, city at 30 pools for 9.5 ms at maximum zoom — same subsystem, fifty times apart
neither author could see it alone, which is the argument for it belonging in the package: an exhibit measures its own scene and cannot know it is on the wrong side of a quadratic
city’s workaround divides the caller’s LightFieldOpts.scale by the zoom: 18.1 ms to 8.6 ms at 2.6x
interacts with scale being a live panel knob, so a compensation folded in silently would fight the control the panel exposes — decide the layering deliberately
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city, reconciled against examples/caverns. GALLERY.md § Scale’s lights bullet has been rewritten twice on this and was wrong both times.

tasks.title: polyRamp allocates a gradient on every call, uncached
acceptance: createLinearGradient on every call, with no cache at all — 4,298 allocations per frame measured in examples/city, because post and cylinder are both built on it
same class as K39 and in the same file, but with no cache rather than a broken one, and plausibly the larger number of the two
non-negotiable 7: the hot path allocates nothing
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city, found by the same instrumentation that confirmed K39.

tasks.title: Loop.resetStats is all-or-nothing, so a rolling worst frame costs every other reader
acceptance: GALLERY.md § Scale asks every exhibit for a ROLLING worst frame; the only way to get one today is a timer calling resetStats(), which zeroes fps and frameMs for every other consumer

examples/city’s control panel stat line read 0.0ms · 0fps one second in five, and the exhibit removed knobs.frameTime from the shared panel rather than ship two readouts that disagree — a shared instrument deleted because the stats API could not serve two readers
four exhibits have now built four different instruments for this one number and at least two of them report a figure that is not true
wants a resetWorst(), or a worstFrameMs carrying its own window — the exhibit estimates three lines
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city. Lands with K40 and K43; all three are the same gate being measured by everyone separately.

tasks.title: Camera.zoom is not settable, so framing a deliberate overflow is ceremony
acceptance: GALLERY.md § Scale requires the world to overflow the viewport, and fitBounds is the only door to a zoom
so an exhibit hands fitBounds a viewport-shaped rectangle whose spans are viewport / zoom — the zoom spelled as the number it is — then overwrites the centre it picked
a setZoom(z, anchor) removes the ceremony without weakening the pointer-anchoring rule that made zoom construction-time in the first place
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city while framing to the new § Scale extent row. A rule this repo added made an existing API awkward.

tasks.title: tileBounds' height argument is wrong for a camera fence
acceptance: tileBounds extends minY upward by the height it is given, which is right for framing — the tallest building must fit — and wrong for a fence
passing the map’s tallest building lets a player park the viewport in the sky above the far corner and still satisfy keepVisible
the fit and the fence want different rectangles and there is one function; either it grows a second form or the camera stops taking the same rect for both jobs
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city.

tasks.title: The light field is not occluded, and a night city is its worst case
acceptance: draw declares this as its own largest limitation, and examples/city is the case that makes it visible: a street-level pool composites over the roof of the tower in front of it, so a dense block grows pale ellipses fourteen storeys up
the exhibit got from ~130 pools to ~30 with halved radii, and measured scale: 1 as buying nothing but 5 ms

not fixable from an exhibit. Decide whether it is fixable at all, or whether the answer is a documented placement discipline — a pool whose footprint reaches a roofline behind it is a placement error rather than an engine limitation
observed still visible in the shipped opening frame, so whatever is decided has to be checkable
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/city; confirmed by the orchestrator looking at the opening frame.

tasks.title: PathFinder's heuristic ignores weights, so any weighted map costs 17x
acceptance: the octile heuristic carries no weight term, so any TileCost above 1 makes the estimate inadmissible-by-underestimate and slides A* toward Dijkstra
measured on identical geometry in examples/clay: 0.13 ms mean unweighted against 2.18 ms weighted, with an 8.9 ms worst
weights are this package’s own documented way to express "shorter but harder", so the feature and the performance of the feature disagree
scaling the estimate by the map’s minimum weight is admissible and free
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/clay, the first exhibit to re-plan against a map that changes under it. Forced the exhibit to bake its cost grid into a Uint8Array to afford re-planning at all. Closed 2026-08-18: PathOptions.minWeight scales the octile estimate; 6.8x on a uniform-weighted map, optimality checked against FlowField.

tasks.title: tileSourceOf answers has() true everywhere, so a height pick never misses
acceptance: correct for an unbounded world, and screenToTileOnHeights uses has() as its ONLY off-map test
so the naive composition of the two returns a grid coordinate for a tap on the sky — examples/clay reports sculpting grid (-4000, 900) from one
a boundedTileSource(get, w, h) closes it; every bounded-heightfield exhibit currently writes the same six lines by hand
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/clay. Two correct decisions composing into a wrong answer, which is the class this repo keeps finding.

tasks.title: ui has no button, toggle, segmented control or slider
acceptance: canyon needed a slider and hand-wrote an <input type=range> with ~35 lines of vendor-pseudo-element CSS; clay needed a raise/cut toggle and hand-wrote that
in both cases the missing primitive was the exhibit’s ONE control — the thing the whole exhibit is operated by
GALLERY.md rule 7 says an exhibit that finds it easier to draw its readouts into the canvas has found something. Two exhibits, two different missing primitives, is that finding twice
decide deliberately: either ui grows input primitives, or rule 7 is amended to say controls are the exhibit’s own and only readouts are ui’s
tasks.notes: Filed independently by examples/canyon and examples/clay.

tasks.title: A bounded square map has a minimum size, and it is not in the document
acceptance: a square grid projects to a diamond, and a viewport inscribed in it needs w <= 2H - 4h

examples/clay at 96 tiles: 3,044 px against a 2,939 px frame — satisfiable at exactly one camera position, which produces § Scale’s named "hard corner with background behind it" and no way to pan out of it
the exhibit’s map is 160 tiles for this reason rather than for the extent row, which means § Scale is currently taking credit for arithmetic it does not state
any exhibit sizing a bounded square map should do this first; it belongs beside the extent row
tasks.notes: Filed by examples/clay. A constraint § Scale implies and never spells out.

tasks.title: The Chrome consent question is a dead end in a non-interactive session
acceptance: found in the first blind e2e run: codex exec ran the preflight correctly, found no Chrome, printed the consent sentence verbatim, and stopped — which is right in a session with a human and fatal in one without
a headless invocation (codex exec, grok -p, claude --print) has no second turn, so the question is asked into a void and the run ends having built nothing
the preflight must detect that nobody can answer — no TTY, or a single-turn invocation — and proceed with the warning STATED rather than ASKED
the contract is unchanged for an interactive user: warn, ask once, never refuse. This adds the third case, which is warn, do not ask, and say plainly in the final report that nothing was looked at
the same hazard applies to the non-empty-directory question, which is the other place the parent skill blocks on an answer
tasks.notes: Found by the blind validation run on 2026-08-18, in exactly the environment the run existed to test. The skill behaved correctly by its own specification; the specification did not contemplate an agent with no user attached. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: preflight now warns-and-proceeds where nobody can answer; detection is positive-evidence rather than a TTY check.

tasks.title: An agent picked 'ink' as a roof colour and got black buildings
acceptance: found in the blind e2e run: codex wrote isoRoof(..., seed % 2 ? 'warn' : 'ink'), so half the market's roofs render near-black and the town reads as burnt
'ink' is the outline and text slot. Nothing in its name says so, and a slot list read by an agent choosing a roof colour offers it beside 'warn' and 'ground' as an equal
the art skill must name which slots are FILLS and which are OUTLINES, in a table, before it lists any of them
this is the sharpest evidence yet for the looking loop: a black roof is invisible to a compiler, passes every test, and is obvious in one glance. Codex could not look, and shipped it
tasks.notes: Found by the blind validation run on 2026-08-18. The agent did nothing unreasonable — it read a slot list and chose a name. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: skills/art opens with a fills-versus-outlines slot table verified against draw shade()/outlineOf().

tasks.title: The scale doctrine does not reach an agent building from one sentence
acceptance: the market square built blind is a diorama: a small world dead centre, visible corners on all four sides, and roughly two thirds of the opening frame empty background
that is precisely the failure docs/GALLERY.md § Scale exists to name, and every exhibit in this repo was rebuilt against it
none of that reasoning is in the skills. The gallery paid for it over eleven exhibits and the plugin ships without it
§ Scale's five rows — extent, fill, edges, density, cost — belong in the skills as the shape a first build should take, not as a rule an author is graded against afterwards
tasks.notes: Found by the blind validation run. The kit knows this and the product does not. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: the starting boot ships a 160-tile map with an opening rect; measured 3480x1773 against a 1440x900 frame.

tasks.title: The preflight asks for one instrument when it needs any instrument
acceptance: the preflight tests for the Claude in Chrome extension and, finding none, warns that the game cannot be looked at
in the blind run Claude noticed Chrome itself was installed, drove it with puppeteer-core, and looked at its game repeatedly — the check said no and the answer was yes

it found four defects that way, every one invisible to a compiler: a viewport fitted to a tile rectangle so half the frame was empty ocean, a HUD reading the night ink so three rows were black on black, light pools landing at the summit elevation 200px up-screen from the water they were meant to show, and a flat relight price that made letting every beacon die the cheapest way to play
so the preflight must ask whether ANY instrument is reachable — the extension, a local Chrome through puppeteer or CDP, a headless browser — and only warn when none is
the warning is still correct when nothing is available. It was wrong here, and being wrong in the pessimistic direction cost the user nothing only because the agent ignored it
tasks.notes: Found by the blind validation run on 2026-08-18. The one agent that could look shipped a markedly better game than the one that could not, and it could look because it disagreed with our own preflight. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: preflight asks whether any rung of the looking ladder is reachable, not just the extension.

tasks.title: An author checks the hour that flatters the scene
acceptance: third instance of one shape: Lamp Road opened at night and was a black screen; a stranger built an orchard and verified it at "Dawn mist", where it is lovely; the harness caught a later phase at 84% near-black and 98% of the border
a day cycle has a worst hour and an author sees whichever one is on screen when they look
looking.md must say to sample a cycle at both ends rather than once
look.mjs wants a way to force a phase — an --at or --advance flag — so the check is deliberate rather than whatever the clock happened to be doing
tasks.notes: Found by the round-three blind run. The agent looked, and looked at the right thing, at the wrong time. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: looking.md says sample both ends; look.mjs gained --advance/--at and finds the orchard dark phase on demand.

tasks.title: The agent with the best looking loop still shipped an unreadable HUD
acceptance: Claude drove a browser, fixed four defects by looking, and shipped a HUD whose text measures 1.58 to 2.53 against its own backdrop — every row under the 4.5 floor
the harness caught all five nodes; the eye did not, because low contrast reads as atmosphere rather than as a defect and the world behind it was beautiful
so contrast is the measure that must not be left to judgement. The hud skill needs the floor stated as a number, and the instruction to read it off the harness rather than to eyeball it
this is the counterpart to the ink slot finding: that one made a fill unreadable, this one makes text unreadable, and both are invisible to a compiler
tasks.notes: Found by the round-three blind run. The most capable agent, with the loop running, still missed it — which is the argument for a number over an opinion. Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the tree: skills/hud states 4.5 as a number and points at the harness legibility row; paletteVars case quantified.

tasks.title: from-one-sentence/ is evidence — preserved as built, and not to be tidied
acceptance: three games built by three vendors' agents from one sentence each, in an empty directory, with no access to this repository. Chime Path (Claude), Evenfall Orchard (Codex), Before the Bell (Grok)

DO NOT EDIT THE GAME SOURCE. Not src/, not index.html, not tsconfig.json, not the lockfiles. Their whole value is that nobody designed them and nobody polished them. A tidy-up is a deletion of the evidence, not an improvement to it

DO NOT convert @latticekit/* to workspace:*. Every lockfile resolves to registry.npmjs.org at 0.1.0, and that is the artifact — it is what a stranger's install produces. A local path would make these ordinary in-repo examples
DO NOT add them to the root workspaces array. Membership would make a root npm install resolve @latticekit/* to packages/* and perform exactly the conversion above, silently, as a side effect

the two known defects stay: Evenfall Orchard's day cycle goes 84% near-black at one phase (#181820, verified today), and Chime Path's five HUD nodes measure 1.58-2.53 contrast under a 4.5 floor. Both are named in from-one-sentence/README.md. A record that hides its blemishes is not a record
they are not gallery exhibits and are not bound by the line rule or GALLERY.md section Scale. npm run gallery reports nineteen and must keep reporting nineteen
the only change made to them was the --port number in each dev script, because Chime Path shipped on 5183 and the other two both on 5173. They are 5210, 5211 and 5212 now
tasks.notes: Moved out of /tmp/lattice-e2e-v3 on 2026-08-18 and preserved verbatim. All three build (tsc --noEmit && vite build) and serve; all three pass anything/framing/motion/console under tools/looking/look.mjs, and Chime Path fails legibility on purpose because that failure is the record. Session transcripts and the round-three brief are in from-one-sentence/transcripts/. Deliberately outside npm run verify — the reasoning, and the accepted residual risk that they can rot unnoticed, is written out in from-one-sentence/README.md.

tasks.title: A recording started mid-game cannot be verified, and the verdict names nothing
acceptance: three packages hold three positions on where a replay index starts: loop.replay always starts at 0 and has no startTick; input.replayCursor deliberately rebases to the driver index and names a mid-game recording as the case where they differ; persist stores absolute ticks and requires startTick
probed on a session recorded from tick 40 for 12 ticks: loop reports ticks 12, checkpoints 0, divergedAt -1; persist reports matched false, checkpointsChecked 0, divergence null, refused null
matched:false with no divergence and no refusal violates ReplayVerdict own rule that a refusal is never a pass and the field that differed is named. Nothing is named
it fails safe rather than reporting a confident wrong answer, and it fails silently, and two packages advertise a path the third makes unverifiable
deliberately not encoded as a test: a test asserting the current behaviour would pin the defect
owner is most likely loop, as the package that cannot express a non-zero starting index. Alternatives: persist rebases checkpoint ticks by startTick, or input and persist agree startTick is always 0
tasks.notes: Found by C12 while writing the four cross-package contract tests — a contract this repository has asserted since its design phase, tested for the first time on 2026-08-19, and found already broken at the seam none of the three suites can see.

tasks.title: rng.float checks its bounds and not its span, so it returns the Infinity its own doc exists to prevent
acceptance: createRng('x').float(-Number.MAX_VALUE, Number.MAX_VALUE) returns Infinity; with a draw of exactly 0 the same expression is NaN, because min + 0 * Infinity is NaN
both bounds pass expectFinite — max - min is what overflows, and nothing checks it

the method's own doc says it throws 'unless both bounds are finite' precisely because 'an infinite bound would produce Infinity or NaN, and JSON.stringify writes both as null — a value that vanishes from a save with the checksum still matching'
a check that passes when it should fail, in the package that owns determinism, on the exact value SEAMS names as undetectable downstream
fix is one line: expectFinite(max - min, 'rng.float(max - min)') after the two bound checks
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-1. No call site in the kit reaches it — medium rather than low because the guard is specifically the one claiming to close this door.

tasks.title: PoolOptions is write-only, against non-negotiable 11
acceptance: max, checked, initial, create and reset all go into new Pool({…}) and none comes back out; size and free are derived counters, not the options
a debug overlay drawing 'particles: 312 / 512' must hold its own copy of 512, which is the shadow copy the rule exists to remove
settability is a separate question — max is a cost value read on the acquire path — but reading it back is free and has no counter-argument
same defect as K14 (iso camera), K18 (audio), K19 and K34 (draw); core is the package all four sit on
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-2.

tasks.title: Pool.release accepts an instance the pool never made, and both counters then lie
acceptance: release() pushes whatever it is handed onto the free list without incrementing #created, so after one foreign release size is 2, free is 3, and size - free is -1
free's own doc says 'size - free is how many are out'; a negative answer means the leak assertion the module is built around has stopped working
max stops bounding: a pool with max 2 hands out three instances, and max's doc is the argument that it must not

checked: true does not catch it — indexOf finds nothing, because the foreign object is not yet on the free list, and checked's doc calls what it catches 'the single nastiest bug this module can cause'
the module already says a released instance must not be touched again; what it does not say is that a wrong release corrupts the counters rather than being ignored
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-3. Caller discipline, but the symptom presents nowhere near the release that caused it.

tasks.title: The Pool constructor reports the caller’s mistake under a method the caller never called
acceptance: new Pool({ create, initial: -1 }) throws 'pool.preallocate: expected a non-negative integer count, got -1' — the word `initial` appears nowhere, and `preallocate` appears nowhere in the caller's code
same for new Pool({ max: 2, initial: 5 }), which reports capacity arithmetic under preallocate
create and max are validated in the constructor and read correctly; initial is the one delegated, and the delegation leaks the callee’s name
non-negotiable 9: an error names the caller’s mistake, never a message that only makes sense with the source open beside it

packages/core/test/pool.test.ts:184 pins the message verbatim for a direct preallocate(-1) call, which is correct — so the fix is a label parameter, not a change to preallocate’s own message. The constructor case is asserted with toThrow(RangeError) alone, so the wrong label is untested exactly where it is wrong
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-4. A test currently defends the defect in one direction and is silent in the other.

tasks.title: rng.weighted overflows its total silently and then always returns the last row
acceptance: rng.weighted([1e308, 1e308, 1e308]) returns index 2 on every one of twenty consecutive draws — three equal weights, one outcome, forever
total saturates to Infinity, target = next() * Infinity is Infinity, every target < accumulated test is false, and the loop falls through to `return last`
the doc enumerates three throw conditions — empty, a negative or non-finite entry, sums to zero — and the fourth, sums above the finite range, is missing
a deterministic wrong distribution is worse than a non-deterministic one: it will never be caught by a repeated run
sim explicitly declines to cap measured quantities (“1e40 is a perfectly good double”), so a huge weight is not absurd in this genre
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-5. Low: I could not construct a weight table in this repo that reaches it.

tasks.title: The -0 defense is applied in two places and skipped in the five that produce one
acceptance: noise.unsignZero and v2Perp’s `0 - ay` both exist because JSON.stringify(-0) is "0" and a persisted value would come back different from the one that went in
v2Scale(out, {x:0,y:0}, -1) yields -0 on both components — reflecting a zero velocity on a bounce is the plausible route
lerp(-0,-0,1), moveTowards(0,-0,1), clamp(-0,-5,5) and v2Lerp over -0 endpoints all return -0

hashNumber(-0) === hashNumber(0), so a hashed digest is unaffected; the damage is confined to Object.is and strict-equality comparisons, and to persist, which never calls expectSerializable at all (see L9)

decide whether the defense is the callee’s job (unsignZero everywhere a zero can be signed) or the boundary’s (expectSerializable at the write) — a defense applied in two of seven places reads to the next author as one that is not needed
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-6. This is a decision, not a patch; that is why it is a task.

tasks.title: The Tier B linter cannot see the operator form of pow, and there is a live undeclared site
acceptance: the rule is one regex over Math.(sin|cos|tan|asin|acos|atan|atan2|pow|exp|log|log2|log10|cbrt|hypot|sinh|cosh|tanh); `a ** b` is Number::exponentiate, which ECMA-262 defines as implementation-approximated — identical standing to Math.pow — and matches nothing
Math.expm1, Math.log1p, Math.asinh, Math.acosh and Math.atanh are also unlisted and also implementation-approximated
packages/audio/src/voice.ts:84 is a live undeclared Tier B site today: `hz * SEMITONE ** semitones`. It is a frequency and never reaches a save, so the consequence is nil and the rule is not

AGENTS.md: the marker exists “so that every one of them is greppable, so an auditor can ask of each in turn whether it ever reaches a save file” — the operator form is not greppable by the mechanism the constitution names
found only by writing a second scanner; a rule whose enforcement has a hole is a rule that is followed until the first hurry
tasks.notes: C1. docs/audit/core.md § CORE-8. Routed out of core: the defect is in tools/ and the live site is in audio/, neither of which the auditor owned.

tasks.title: The checksum covers the payload and not the envelope, so v, t and n are unprotected
acceptance: store.ts justifies `d` being a string with “the checksum then covers the exact bytes read”; it covers the exact bytes of the payload, and the three header fields that decide which migrations run, how much offline time is owed, and who wins a cross-tab race sit outside it

v tampered up (one character, checksum untouched): reason future, quarantined false, status refusing-newer, writable false, every save skipped not-writable for the life of the install, rejected() null, and the message asserts “the player has an older deploy” — which is false and sends the reader to the deploy pipeline

v tampered down: the save re-runs the whole chain. With the loose recognizers migrate.ts advises, gold 100 comes back 200 with source save, failure null, migratedFrom 1 — a double migration no layer detects
t tampered: elapsedSince reports 19,676 days of offline gap with failure null; elapsedSince is deliberately unclamped from above because the cap is sim’s decision
fix shape: checksum `${v}|${t}|${n}|${d}`. It is a format change, so it needs its own rung and a read-both-ways window — which is why this is an architect task and not a builder one
a cheaper partial fix that needs no format change is L15 (bound v)
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-1. The checksum is currently a payload checksum wearing an envelope checksum’s job description.

tasks.title: Infinity, NaN and -0 are laundered by the write path with a valid checksum, and nothing in the package looks
acceptance: store.save({ gold: Infinity, ratio: NaN, neg: -0 }) reports written true; the disk holds "gold":null,"ratio":null,"neg":0 with a valid checksum; open() returns source save, failure null
SEAMS.md names this exact value as the one that “does not survive being written down… with a valid checksum, so no layer downstream can detect it”

core ships expectSerializable for it and says where the check belongs: “at the moment of writing rather than the moment of reading”. persist imports isSerializable and applies it only to the envelope’s own t and n in inspect(). envelopeText() applies neither to the payload
the whole defense is delegated to a game-written recognizer on the read path, one save too late — by which time the real value is gone

Infinity appears zero times across packages/persist/test/*.ts; the only place in the repo that gets it right is examples/migration/src/chain.ts, a game-layer recognizer in an exhibit built to demonstrate the trap

this is a policy decision, not a one-liner: walking the whole state every four seconds costs real time on a phone. Candidates: refuse in envelopeText with a new WriteFailure.reason; compare JSON.parse(d) against the input; or StoreOptions.strictNumbers defaulting on in development. Someone has to choose — today nobody has
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-2. The hardest failure in the kit to diagnose from a bug report, in the one package positioned to make it impossible.

tasks.title: A non-finite now() writes an envelope the store reads back as malformed, and the message blames a third party
acceptance: with now: () => Infinity, save() reports written true and the disk holds "t":null

the next open() degrades to fresh with reason malformed and the message “Something else has written to this key” — the store produced a save only it could have produced, cannot read it, and reports it as somebody else’s doing
inspect() applies asEpochMillis on the way in and validates t with isSerializable; envelopeText() writes t: now() raw
createStore already validates that now is a function; it does not validate what it returns, at the one call per write where it costs one comparison
StoreOptions.now is typed Now so this needs a cast or an untyped JavaScript caller — which is exactly the population expectSerializable, asEpochMillis and expectObject are each documented for
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-3. Every subsequent boot degrades to fresh and quarantines the evidence.

tasks.title: The autosave interval is measured on the calendar clock, so a backwards clock jump stalls it silently
acceptance: Autosave.tick() subtracts two EpochMillis and compares against minWriteIntervalMs; core/time.ts says an EpochMillis “can also jump backwards… anything that subtracts two of these must tolerate a negative result”, and tick() does not

reproduced: after a -1h step, ten consecutive tick() calls across ten simulated minutes all return false, status stays ok, writable stays true, lastWrite still shows the previous success, and the disk does not change
the stall lasts as long as the jump; setting a clock forward to skip a build timer and then back is a first-class idle-game behavior, and time.ts names it
not high only because flush() is on a different path — installFlushTriggers still writes on visibilitychange and pagehide, so the loss is bounded to a crash or a kill. Nothing reports the condition

the fix is not a monotonic clock — a second clock in this package would break the one-clock rule. Treat a negative elapsed as “the interval has passed”: at - lastAttemptAt < minWriteIntervalMs && at >= lastAttemptAt
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-4.

tasks.title: StoreOptions, AutosaveOptions and RecorderOptions are all write-only, against non-negotiable 11
acceptance: StoreOptions has 13 fields and Store reads back two of them (key, and version via chain.head). minWriteIntervalMs, maxBytes, conflict, quarantine, checksum, adapter, chain, fresh, now, onFailure and onWriteError are all unreadable
AutosaveOptions.schedule is not on Autosave; RecorderOptions’ six fields are not on Recorder

durable is the sharpest case: a game wants to tell a private-mode player at the door, which is the package’s own argument for the field, and cannot ask until after open() — or must decode it out of status, which encodes two other conditions and is documented as being masked by them
minWriteIntervalMs is the second: a settings panel offering “save every N seconds” must hold its own copy of N, and two copies drift
settability is separate and mostly answers baked — chain, adapter and key are identity; checksum is record. The finding is only about reading, where there is no counter-argument
fourth package with this defect after K14, K18, K19/K34
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-5.

tasks.title: createRecorder validates the two options that cannot hurt and neither of the two that can
acceptance: a Digest returning Infinity is a legal Tier A result — SEAMS says so — and becomes null once the log is stored, so the verifier reports divergence { expected: null, actual: Infinity } over a run that did not diverge
Divergence.expected is typed number and is not one; replay.ts’s own header says a report nobody should trust “puts the determinism claim back where it started while looking like it has been tested”
digests run on 1 tick in 600, so expectSerializable(digest(state), ’recorder.digest’) costs nothing measurable

RecorderOptions.rng is not validated either: { seed: -1, state: 1e21 } is sealed into a log and surfaces much later as “Rng.fromSnapshot: expected uint32 seed and state”, naming core’s function rather than the option that was wrong (non-negotiable 9)
replay.ts calls rng the thing that makes a replay work, and it is the only recorder option not checked, while digest-is-a-function and checkpointEvery-is-a-positive-integer both are

Recorder.mark also accepts a fractional or negative tick, which no verifier can ever match because mark compares checkpoint.tick !== tick exactly; SEAMS pins the tick index as starting at 0 and incrementing by exactly one
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-6 and § PERSIST-8. Distinct from K62, which covers matched:false with nothing named for a mid-game recording.

tasks.title: With conflict: 'refuse', a tab that loses once can never write again
acceptance: sequence only advances on a successful write and conflicted() compares against it, so once another tab is ahead the losing store is permanently mute: five consecutive save() calls all return skipped conflict
the losing store reports status ok and writable true the whole time, while writing nothing, forever
the only recovery is open(), which replaces the live state with what is on disk — so a game following the documentation has no non-destructive path back
the option’s doc explains what ’refuse’ detects and stops there; the missing half is what a game is supposed to do on the second conflict
the argument for detection-not-locking is right and is not what this asks to change
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-7.

tasks.title: The envelope’s v is unbounded, so damage to it is indistinguishable from a newer deploy
acceptance: Number.isInteger(1e21) is true, so "v":1e21 and "v":2**53 both pass inspect() and read as future — permanently read-only, nothing quarantined
core ships expectSafeInteger for exactly the “this number has left the exactly-representable integers” case and it is not applied here
a sanity bound on v — 0 <= v <= head + some slack — turns most corruptions of that field into malformed, which is quarantined and does degrade to fresh
cheap, needs no format change, and closes the worst half of L8(a) on its own
tasks.notes: C7. docs/audit/persist.md § PERSIST-9.

tasks.title: An autosave armed before open() re-arms forever, and quarantine keeps only the last bad boot
acceptance: makeAutosave calls arm() regardless of phase, so a handle created on a store in phase new schedules a write, the write reports closed, and the callback re-arms — a fresh timer every cycle for the life of the page
not a leak of any size, but the package’s own position is that “a package that creates a timer is a package that owns a leak”, and stop() is the only exit with nothing telling a caller they need it

separately: quarantine writes to one key, so a boot loop over a broken save overwrites the first piece of evidence on the second boot — while Rejected’s doc argues that degrading without keeping the bytes “destroys the only copy of the bug that just ate a player’s campus”
both are small; they are filed together because they are the same file and the same review
